qt: to the Commission Anna Bryłka (PfE) Subject:

Since mid-July, the Black Sea has been blockaded due to Russian attacks on merchant ships. According to information from Ukraine, consultations are ongoing with frontline countries and the EU regarding the transit of agricultural goods and increasing exports to the EU market. In this connection: Is the Commission consulting frontline countries regarding the import of agricultural goods from Ukraine, with a view to preventing a grain crisis such as the one we faced in 2022 and 2023?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.11.2026) In response to the intensified attacks on the Ukrainian Black Sea ports, within the Solidarity Lanes initiative the Commission has engaged in regular discussions with the authorities and stakeholders from Ukraine, Moldova and neighbouring EU countries in order to identify the needs related to alternative logistics routes for Ukrainian exports and imports – both agricultural and non-agricultural. This includes transit via the EU to/from third countries via the European ports. Special focus within the Solidarity Lanes is given on the Danube corridor (via Moldova, Romania, Ukrainian Danube ports, and the port of Constanta), which presents the most promising alternative in terms of capacity potential, and is the most cost-effective route as compared to the Black Sea. The usage of this corridor for Ukrainian grain export has increased since July 2026, and its capacity could be further expanded if market demand occurs. The Commission is also monitoring the needs for Ukrainian exports and imports via other alternative routes, in close collaboration with relevant authorities. So far, the Solidarity Lanes have met the market demand for cargo transport to and from Ukraine. The Commission continues to monitor EU-Ukraine trade flows. In this regard, the revised EU Ukraine Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area (DCFTA)1, in force since 29 October 2025, provides for a predictable and balanced framework. Trade data so far proves the fair and balanced nature of the revised DCFTA.
